tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with 'Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review', which is imperative phrasing focused on user intent. It explicitly enumerates many trigger contexts (high/low bills, token drift, pricing tiers, PT idle/oversized, quota headroom, throttling, etc.) covering edge cases where users don't name the domain directly, and ends with an explicit exclusion ('Not for outages happening now'). While dense, it remains a single flowing sentence/paragraph rather than verbose prose.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review, for example why the bill is high or suspiciously low...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and almost entirely domain-specific: exact API fields, metric names, quota semantics, and precise disambiguations (e.g. us./eu./global. profile billing). There is virtually no explanation of generic concepts the agent already knows.
tests.evidence: "Usage types vary (`-mantle-`, `-standard`, `-flex`, `-priority`, `-cross-region-global`): match a model's lines loosely."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed lookup tables (quota codes, alarm thresholds, cost analysis derivations) are kept in references/ files, and the body only contains routing tables and short rules that link out rather than embedding full reference content.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ (api-quirks.md, checks-model-invocation.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, collection-reference.md, cost-analysis.md, metrics-and-logs.md, quota-codes.md, related-skills.md) has a markdown link in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Reference links are consistently paired with specific trigger conditions (step numbers, check-ids, or 'before interpreting a response').
tests.evidence: "[cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) (Steps 3–5, before any LLM-COST or LLM-PT finding); [checks-model-invocation.md](references/checks-model-invocation.md) (before LLM-INV-002/007)"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, high-risk operations (quota codes, pricing sources, billed-vs-estimated labeling) are given exact, prescriptive rules, while judgment-based tasks (deciding LLM-COST-003/004 applicability, scoping regions) are described with reasoning and flexibility rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: "decide 003/004 from the invocation pattern and the stated workload, at catalog severity" vs "Take the code from the user, from earlier in this review, or from quota-codes.md ... one GetServiceQuota, returned name checked. Never a remembered or guessed code."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple price/data sources exist, the skill gives an explicit priority order rather than a flat menu of equal options.
tests.evidence: "Rates, in order: the user (say so); pricing:GetProducts ... or the pricing page read with verify_aws_claim."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable, repeatable procedure for any Bedrock cost/capacity review (scope, tokens, cost model, coverage check, checks, PT, headroom, alarms) rather than declaring the outcome for one specific instance.
tests.evidence: "Step 1: Scope: region(s), window, models and profiles... Step 8: Assemble the findings, then run \"Before You Present\"."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section plus 'Guardrails — details' documenting specific, non-obvious environment pitfalls (e.g., ACTIVE status misleading, us. profile billing, EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage misreads).
tests.evidence: "'A `us.` profile bills as us-east-1.' It is a geographic routing scope; billing follows the source region"

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: A report template is provided and referenced for full reports, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline templates exist in the body; the report template itself is stored in assets/ and only linked.
tests.evidence: The body contains no inline multi-section report skeleton; it only links to "[capacity-cost-report-template.md](assets/capacity-cost-report-template.md)".

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file capacity-cost-report-template.md is linked in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies the condition for loading it (only for a full report), satisfying the when-to-load requirement.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with no absolute path or traversal.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow ('Procedure — Capacity & Cost Review') is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, matching the required format.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: **Scope:** region(s), window, models and profiles..." through "- [ ] Step 8: Assemble the findings..."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own output against rules before presenting.
tests.evidence: "## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output\n\nA confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can't be met, say so."
